Area.evidence_source: The third main topic in the interviews was that of the informants' experiences of their relationships with the elderly people, in which distance is frequently described. Some of the elderly had good contacts within their family, and some were portrayed as caring parents and grandparents, but most of the accounts characterize the relationships as distant. Many informants also expressed the relationship as difficult. The main impression was that the elderly had shown strong self-control and reserve on an emotional level. This affected how the informants viewed the elderly and how they felt the elderly regarded them. These aspects of the informants' relationships with the elderly can be described in two sub-topics, the titles of which are quotes from the informants: 'I didn't know him' and 'He showed no ability to meet us halfway'.
